Title: Text Area input is automatically converted from uppercase to sentence case after submission
Steps to Reproduce:
# Navigate to the form page.
# Enter the value **"QA"** in the first (mandatory) Text Area.
# Leave the other fields as desired.
# Click the **Submit** button.
# Observe the submitted value displayed on the page.
Expected Result: The entered value should be displayed exactly as entered by the user (**"QA"**), without any modification of letter casing.
Actual Result:
The entered value **"QA"** is displayed as **"Qa"** after form submission.

*Additional Observation:*
The issue occurs with any word entered entirely in uppercase letters. After submission, only the first character remains uppercase while all remaining characters are automatically converted to lowercase.

*Examples:*

* Input: **QA** - Displayed: **Qa**
* Input: **TESTING** - Displayed: **Testing**
* Input: **BUG** - Displayed: **Bug**

*Impact:*
The application alters user-provided data and does not preserve the original input format, which may lead to incorrect data representation.

Title: Cancel button does not display the user's input from the prompt
Steps to Reproduce:
# Navigate to the page.
# Click the **Click** button.
# Observe that an alert/prompt window is displayed.
# Enter any text in the input field, for example **"QA Testing"**.
# Click the **Cancel** button.
# Observe the message displayed on the page.
Expected Result:
After clicking **Cancel**, the text entered by the user in the prompt input field should be displayed on the page, according to the requirement:

*"The user's input should be displayed on the page."*
Actual Result:
After clicking **Cancel**, the user's input is not displayed. Instead, the page displays the message:

*"You cancel the prompt"*

For example:

* Input: **QA Testing**
* Click: **Cancel**
* Expected output: **QA Testing**
* Actual output: **You cancel the prompt**

*Additional Information:*
When the user clicks **OK**, the entered text is correctly displayed on the page. The issue occurs only when the **Cancel** button is used.

*Impact:*
The application does not behave consistently between the **OK** and **Cancel** actions and does not satisfy the requirement that the user's input should be displayed after closing the prompt.

Title: Bottom square can be dragged multiple times if not dropped onto the top square
Severity: Minor (functional, not blocking, but violates stated requirement)
Steps to Reproduce:
# Go to [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/boxes|smart-link] 
# Drag the bottom square ("Drag me") to any location that is **not** the top square ("Drop here")
# Release the mouse — the square stays where dropped
# Repeat step 2–3 multiple times, dragging the square to different empty areas
# Observe how many times the drag can be repeated
Expected Result: Per the stated requirement, the bottom square should only be draggable once — implying that after the first drag (or first drag attempt), further dragging should be disabled or ignored, regardless of where it lands.
Actual Result:
The square can be dragged an unlimited number of times, as long as it is not dropped onto the top square. The "once only" restriction is only enforced once the square is successfully dropped on the top square (triggering "Dropped!"), not on the act of dragging itself.

*Additional Notes:*
This suggests the "drag count" or "locked" state is being set only inside the successful-drop event handler, rather than on drag start/end in general. If the intent was "the user gets one shot at placing it," the fix should track drag attempts (or lock the element after the first drag interaction) rather than only locking on successful drop.

Title: Double-clicking the smiley moves it between squares without updating "Dropped!" text, leaving text behind in the wrong square
Steps to Reproduce:
# Go to [https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|https://www.qa-practice.com/elements/dragndrop/images|smart-link] 
# Drag the smiley into a square; confirm "Dropped!" appears there correctly
# Double-click the smiley (see attachments).
# Observe the smiley's position and the "Dropped!" text's position
# Repeat drag + double-click a few times
Expected Result: Either double-click has no effect, or if it moves the smiley, "Dropped!" text moves with it to the correct square.
Actual Result:
Double-clicking moves the smiley to the other square, but "Dropped!" text stays behind in the square the smiley left. Repeating the action causes the text to keep lagging one square behind the smiley's actual position — resulting in a square showing "Dropped!" with no smiley present.

*Additional Notes:* Suggests double-click is bound to a separate handler that moves the element without triggering the same drop-state update as the drag-and-drop flow. Worth a quick check on other click interactions too.

*Related issues:* See MFW-51 — same page/feature, different root cause.
